A map of central Nigeria in the 19th century showing the Nupe Emirate. The Niger River flows through the centre. The city of Bida is clearly marked with a star as the capital. Arrows point outwards from Bida to the south and southeast (towards Kabba, Lokoja, and the Niger-Benue confluence) to show the direction of Nupe expansion.

A 19th-century illustration-style depiction of the Nupe brass-smiths at work. Two men sit under a thatched roof, hammering intricate patterns into large brass trays and bowls. In the background, a local market scene showing traders exchanging goods. Clean flat textbook style, warm earthy colours, white background.
